subject: Tactical OKR course-correct: throughput & QBR artifacts
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Tactical OKR course-correct: throughput & QBR artifacts

Team —

Quick mid-quarter pulse ahead of next week's QBR prep: overall we're tracking off-plan on two priority OKRs that intersect the Serving Runtime and Dedicated capacity workstreams. I wanted to surface status, propose a short re-scope, and call out concrete dependency asks so we can finalize the QBR slides by Friday.

Status highlights
- OKR: Reduce p99 generation latency for hosted API from 420ms -> 320ms. Current: ~385ms (15% work remaining; poking at kernel selection and KV cache TTL).
- OKR: Lower per-token cost for high-throughput workloads by 12%. Current: 7% improvement (need batching/quantization config for two large customers to get to target).
- QBR artifact readiness: slides 1–6 drafted; need consolidated runbook + headcount ask for slide 7.

Proposed tactical re-scope (2-week window)
- Narrow scope on p99: aim for 350ms SLO in the short term (instead of 320ms target). This buys time for the kernel refactor while keeping visible client improvements.
- Prioritize 2 customers (Acme Data, Orion Apps) for early batching rollout instead of broad rollout across all tier-1 customers.

Concrete asks (owners + timeline)
1) Marcus: escalate Dedicated capacity procurement and commitment for +4 GPU nodes for the west region. Need PO in-hand by 2026-07-27 to meet test schedule.
2) Laura: coordinate once-for-all procurement + security checklist for the additional nodes; we need the SOC/attestation packet and a brief security blurb for the QBR slide.
3) Vanessa: own the trimmed rollout plan and update the OKR wording for the QBR deck (I attached a tactical plan draft).
4) All: validate the runbook material in the draft Drive folder (link below) by EOD Thu so we can lock slides on Fri.

Notes: I attached QBR_prep_notes_v2.pdf and the okrs-tactical-plan.xlsx with the specific breakouts and a proposed timeline.

Thanks — short, direct responses welcome.

—
Logan Wright
Head of Product, Inference
Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tactical OKR course-correct: throughput & QBR artifacts

Thanks Logan — good call. A couple of quick reactions and a suggested alternative narrow-scope that keeps momentum without removing client-visible work.

On the p99 re-scope
- I agree we should avoid over-committing. Proposed wording for QBR: "Adjusted short-term SLO: p99 improvement to 350ms with targeted kernel rollout for top-tier customers; full 320ms target remains roadmaped for H2."

On customer prioritization
- Acme Data is already on the pilot path and has agreed to a controlled roll. Let's make Acme the first channel and Orion the fallback (we should aim for Acme in week 1, Orion week 3). I updated the attached tactical plan with that cadence.

Dependency notes
- Marcus: if procurement can only deliver in early August, we need to confirm a temporary capacity fallback (burst in east region) and I can push a customer communication template.
- Laura: we'll need a 1-page security blurb (SOC2 + KV cache access model) for the QBR slide — 2–3 bullets will do.

I've attached a lightly edited plan (okrs-tactical-plan.xlsx) and a one-slide QBR blurb (QBR_prep_notes_v2.pdf edit). Will review Drive artifacts tonight.

On timelines: Can we commit to the PO by Mon (7/27) as Logan requested? If procurement timeline slips, we should flag the QBR slide as "dependency: capacity procurement" rather than an achieved metric.

On style: keep the QBR message crisp — leaders want what changed, next steps, and risks.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Customer & GTM
Redwood Inference

Short update from procurement/security side:
- Procurement has received a draft PO request and is routed to AWS Marketplace for the node purchase. The earliest firm fulfillment estimate I've been given is 2026-08-05; I'll push to accelerate but want to set expectations.
- Security review: our security team reviewed the attachment and asked for two items: (1) a short KV access diagram and (2) confirmation of audit-log retention for the Dedicated pool. I'll pull the two bullets and share a 1-page ready-for-slide blurb by Thu EOD.

Suggested QBR framing (two lines):
- "Progress: p99 latency improved X% via KV cache tuning and batching; tactical SLO set to 350ms pending kernel completion."
- "Risk & mitigation: Dedicated capacity procurement timing remains the main constraint; we have an east-region fallback if west capacity delays persist."

Next steps I own:
- Finalize the procurement schedule and attach PO number to the Drive folder when available.
- Produce the security blurb (SOC2 + audit retention bullets) by Thu EOD.
